user: What is an arraignment?
assistant: An arraignment is a legal proceeding in a criminal case where the defendant is brought to court. During this process, the defendant is informed of the charges against them and their constitutional rights. They are also given the opportunity to hire an attorney. If the defendant cannot afford one, the court may appoint an attorney to represent them.
Additionally, the defendant may be informed about the possibility of being released on their own recognizance or whether they need to post bail in order to be released from custody. Following this information, the defendant enters a plea, which can be guilty, not guilty, or no contest. If the defendant pleads not guilty, a future hearing is scheduled to continue the case.
user: What happens if I plead "Not Guilty"?
assistant: If you plead "Not Guilty," you are denying the charges against you. The case will then be scheduled for a future hearing. During this time, the prosecution and defense attorneys will exchange discovery materials, which include police reports, blood test results, photographs, and other relevant evidence.
Motions may be filed to dismiss the complaint, set aside the case, or suppress evidence. The defendant has the option to change their plea to guilty or no contest, and a hearing will be held to try to resolve the case without going to trial. However, if the case is not resolved, it will proceed to trial.
user: What about "Guilty"?
assistant: Pleading guilty means you are admitting to committing the offense stated on the ticket. By pleading 'guilty,' you acknowledge that you have committed the crime. At this point, any fines, fees, or court-ordered programs imposed by the judge will be established, and the case may be resolved. If the defendant pleads guilty or no contest, the case can potentially be settled during the arraignment.
user: Who decides if the defendant is guilty or not guilty?
assistant: In a misdemeanor jury trial, the jury decides if the defendant is guilty or not guilty.

What is a misdemeanor?
[The End of Current Turn Question]

[The Start of Reference Answer]
A misdemeanor is a type of crime that carries a maximum punishment of either 6 months or 1 year in county jail, and/or a fine of up to $1,000 for most offenses. Examples of misdemeanors include petty theft, vandalism, driving with a suspended license, and drunk driving, among others.
[The End of Reference Answer]

[The Start of Document]
In criminal cases, defendants almost always have the right to a trial by jury, except in infraction cases. In civil matters, there are many types of cases where there is no right to a trial by jury.

Types of Criminal Cases



Infractions 
An infraction is a minor violation. Many traffic violations are infractions.

 Misdemeanors 

A misdemeanor is a crime with a maximum punishment of:

o   Either 6 months or 1 year in a county jail, and/oro   A $1,000 fine (for most misdemeanors).

Lawyers in Criminal Court

In any misdemeanor or felony criminal case (and any infraction where you have been arrested and NOT released on your written notice to appear, on your own recognizance, or after a deposit of bail), you should have a lawyer. You have the right to represent yourself in criminal court in California. BUT because the consequences of a criminal conviction can be so serious and you can end up in jail or prison, it is best if you have a lawyer represent you.

If you cannot afford your own lawyer, the court will appoint a lawyer for you, often a public defender. Make sure you tell the judge at your arraignment that you cannot afford a lawyer.
